questions.say: Good morning. My name is Alice, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about your hometown. Where is your hometown?

questions.text: Is your hometown a quiet place or a busy one?
questions.say: Is your hometown a quiet place or a busy one?

questions.text: Where do people in your hometown meet their friends?
questions.say: Where do people in your hometown meet their friends?

questions.text: What did you enjoy doing in your hometown as a child?
questions.say: What did you enjoy doing in your hometown as a child?

questions.text: What outdoor activities do you enjoy?
questions.say: Now let's move on to talk about outdoor activities. What outdoor activities do you enjoy?

questions.text: Did you spend much time outdoors as a child?
questions.say: Did you spend much time outdoors as a child?

questions.text: Do you prefer outdoor or indoor activities?
questions.say: Do you prefer outdoor or indoor activities?

questions.text: Do you live near the sea?
questions.say: Now let's move on to talk about the sea. Do you live near the sea?

cueCard.topic: Describe a time when you disagreed with someone.
cueCard.explain: and explain how you felt about this disagreement.

questions.text: Describe a time when you disagreed with someone.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a time when you disagreed with someone. You should say: who you disagreed with; what you disagreed about; what happened in the end; and explain how you felt about this disagreement.

questions.text: Do you still have a good relationship with this person?
questions.say: Thank you. Do you still have a good relationship with this person?

questions.text: What do people in families usually disagree about?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a time when you disagreed with someone, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all disagreements. What do people in families usually disagree about?

questions.text: Is it always a bad thing when people disagree?
questions.say: Is it always a bad thing when people disagree?

questions.text: What is the best way to end a disagreement?
questions.say: What is the best way to end a disagreement?

questions.text: Why do people find it difficult to change their opinions?
questions.say: Now let's talk about discussion and debate. Why do people find it difficult to change their opinions?

questions.text: Should schools teach students how to debate?
questions.say: Should schools teach students how to debate?

questions.text: Has the internet made people more or less willing to listen to different opinions?
questions.say: Has the internet made people more or less willing to listen to different opinions?
